A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Late Wenlock sequence on the Midland Platform is a composite of parasequences, which are the product of a series of relative sea-level changes, with three bentonites being identified, two of which are of a mafic composition.

the Late Homerian sequence stratigraphy of the Malvern and Suckley Hills, and the Abberley Hills is comparable with the sequence stratigraphy of other parts of the Midland Platform, and the Homerian of Gotland.
the Homerian Stage in the central part of the Midland Platform is characterized by two major relative sea-level changes, separated by a transgressive episode.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stratigraphic framework established for the Late Wenlock Series in the Malvern Hills, and across the northern Mid-land Platform, can now be applied to sections in the Suckley and Aberyley Hills.
a sequence stratigraphical approach, combined with the use of bentonites, can be used as a tool for correlation of the Homerian Stage across the northern Mid-lands.

the stratigraphic framework established for the Much Wen-lock Limestone Formation and its immediate stratigraphic neighbours, together with the apatite REE signatures obtained from the bentonites, allows for the establishment of correlations across the Midland Platform, and potentially with Gotland.
